title: playable-screen-20of44
queue_order: One binary (this lane's step-1 commit, merged with origin/master), env-only A/B per title: ON queues with no --env (app default); OFF queues --env with all six vars =0. Scope: 20 of pm/playable-accepted.tsv's 44 titles whose ISO is present on the Nova's DEVICE_ISO_ROOT as of this registration (confirmed live against /home/justin/hakux-work/hardware/titlepush/listing-nova.txt, Oct-3, cross-checked against the live device at queue time -- a request.sh queue failure for a missing ISO is itself evidence a title moved off Nova since the listing). The other 24 are on the Thor only; moving them onto the Nova ("shuffle") is lane.local's job, not this lane's grant (memory shuffle-means-onto-the-nova) -- named as a blocker in NOTES.md/PR.md, not run here. 14 of the 20 use their own named route (docs/testing/titles/routes/<name>.route); the other 6 (ToeJam & Earl III, Gunvalkyrie, Halo: Combat Evolved, Panzer Dragoon Orta, NBA Live 2004, Call of Duty 3) have no route in this tree, so they run as a soak to the title screen with --frames-every. Queued in batches of about 10 titles (20 runs), each batch preceded by its own small pilot per the 30-min device-time gate, HAKUX_RELEASE_PRIO=1.
judge: per-title: logcat read for a crash/hang/abort in ON that OFF does not show (fatal); route-frames or --frames-every captures at matched points, compared by region, ON vs OFF (frames); reportasync1010's armed/late counters where GET_REPORT traffic appears in logcat (reports); both arms' perf_regimen.json/telemetry fps, reported not gated (gfps). No single numeric threshold applies across 20 different titles -- each title's own row is read by eye against its own OFF baseline, recorded in docs/lanes/fastpaths1010/NOTES.md and PR.md's screen table.
baseline: Every one of the 20 titles already has an accepted Playable verdict (pm/playable-accepted.tsv) from an earlier run, most on this same Nova, establishing what correct gameplay for that title's route looks like; this screen's OFF arm is that same known-good code path (all six switches at their native C default, off), and ON is the new default. A title regressing between ON and OFF here would be a regression from fastpaths1010's own step-1 commit, not a pre-existing issue the Playable verdict already accepted.
prediction: None of the 20 fail: reportasync1010, texscan1010 (paired with REPORT_ASYNC), drawrec1010 and perdrawon1010 each already screened their own switch (or pair) on some subset of Playable titles or a broader survey without a correctness regression (texscan1010's own finding was a PERFORMANCE regression when TEXSCAN runs alone, not a correctness one, and this toggle never ships TEXSCAN alone). What would refute it: any ON-only crash/hang; any ON-only visual defect in a frame region OFF does not show; a title whose reportasync counters show armed below 100% that OFF's do not (a GET_REPORT race the other three lanes' own survey titles did not happen to hit).
